buzzRounds.topic: Brewers win their first World Series
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday, October 28, in St. Petersburg, Florida, to win the World Series four games to one. Catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP (most valuable player) after eight hits and four runs batted in, and rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt went 2 for 3 with two runs batted in in the clincher.
buzzRounds.whyCare: It is the first championship for a franchise founded in 1969, and Milwaukee went 11-2 in the postseason, including a four-game sweep of the two-time defending champion Dodgers.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: The Brewers won the first World Series in team history, beating the Rays 4-1 in Game 5, and William Contreras was the MVP with eight hits in the series. They went 11-2 in the playoffs and swept the Dodgers along the way.

details.buzz: Contreras was named World Series MVP after collecting eight hits and four runs batted in over the five games.

buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Baseball Writers' Association of America named its award finalists on Monday, November 2. Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski is up for the National League Cy Young Award (best pitcher) against Chris Sale and Cristopher Sánchez, and Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs, Shohei Ohtani of the Dodgers and Brice Turang of the Brewers are the National League MVP finalists. Yordan Alvarez, Junior Caminero and Bobby Witt Jr. are the American League MVP finalists.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Winners come out next week, from Rookie of the Year on November 9 to MVP on November 12, and champion Milwaukee has four finalists across the awards.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Jacob Misiorowski is a Cy Young finalist after leading the majors with a 1.80 earned run average, and Pete Crow-Armstrong is up for MVP after 45 homers and 41 steals. The Cy Young is announced November 11 and the MVP November 12.

lastGame.label: at Tampa Bay Rays, won 4-1 (World Series Game 5)

details.buzz: Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings to win the World Series clincher, after winning the regular-season earned run average title at 1.80.

buzzRounds.topic: Free agency opens with a lockout looming
buzzRounds.whatHappened: Free agency opened at 5 p.m. Eastern on Monday, November 2, with 183 players on the market. Eight players received qualifying offers, one-year offers worth $23.15 million, including Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers, and they have until November 17 to accept.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Baseball's labor contract (the collective bargaining agreement) expires December 1, and MLB is expected to lock out the players when it does, so the next four weeks could decide which teams make moves before a work stoppage.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Free agency opened Monday with 183 players available, and Seiya Suzuki and Jake Bauers each got a $23.15 million qualifying offer. The labor deal expires December 1, and a lockout is expected then.

buzzRounds.topic: Tarik Skubal tops the free agent market
buzzRounds.whatHappened: Tarik Skubal, Detroit's longtime ace, is a free agent after finishing 2026 with the Dodgers, who traded for him during the season. CBS Sports and MLB Trade Rumors both rank him No. 1 on their free agent lists, and CBS calls him the clear best player available.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Because he was traded during the season, he could not receive a qualifying offer, a one-year offer that would have given his old team a draft pick if he signed elsewhere, so nothing holds back his market.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this winter on both CBS Sports' and MLB Trade Rumors' lists, after the Dodgers traded for him from Detroit during the season.
